items.review_rationale: Read the explicit quotient construction of a directed colimit of R-modules, identifying the diagram, direct sum, transition-relation submodule and quotient separately from the category-theoretic universal property.

references.phrase: direct sum ⊕_i M_i of a family of modules
references.context: Finite-support families of elements of the R-modules M_i under componentwise operations, not the unrestricted product
Natural R-linear maps sending a component element into the direct sum

references.phrase: submodule generated by the differences ι_i(m)−ι_j(μ_ij(m))
references.context: Linear span of the relation elements imposing identification along all directed transition maps
R-module whose elements are equivalence classes modulo the generated relation submodule

references.disposition: These are the explicit colimit identification relations, not a claim that every module diagram is a sequential chain.

items.review_rationale: Reviewed indexed module objects, compatible transition maps on comparable indices, identity and composition equations, and the extra directedness property of the preorder; category-general direct system is the correct existing contextual parallel.

references.phrase: direct system over a preorder in a category

references.disposition: These express the diagram's identity/composition coherence and do not impose extra injectivity or surjectivity on the arrows.

items.review_rationale: Read the coequalizer universal property of a parallel pair of arrows in a category, its equality qf=qg, and unique factoring arrow from any other equalizing morphism; did not replace it with a set-theoretic quotient without category assumptions.

references.phrase: category C with objects and arrows

references.context: Two morphisms with the same domain X and codomain Y, available for composition with q:Y→Q
Arrow q:Y→Q whose precomposites with the given parallel arrows are equal
For each h:Y→Z satisfying hf=hg there is exactly one u:Q→Z with h=u∘q

references.disposition: Categorical equality and composition are already part of the category axioms, not an additional algebraic equality theory.

items.review_rationale: Reviewed the field extension E/F, nonzero polynomial f with F-coefficients and its evaluation at α in E, preserving the distinction between an algebraic element and an entire algebraic extension.

references.context: Polynomial ring in one indeterminate over the base field F, including the zero and nonzero polynomials

references.phrase: polynomial evaluation f(α) at element of E
references.context: Substitution of α∈E into polynomial with F coefficients using field inclusion F⊆E

references.disposition: The existential polynomial relation is the defining criterion for algebraicity, not a requirement that α itself be nonzero.
